What the numbers say

For the session of Friday, November 6, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as mixed. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

8 of 26 tickers (31%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 13 of 25 (52%) above their 200-day average. That sits between the model's 30% and 55% breadth thresholds, so breadth alone decides nothing here. On the day 14 rose and 12 fell; the median move was +0.52%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Technology had the strongest average move at +4.10% and Healthcare the weakest at −1.88%, a spread of 5.98 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 3.46 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

4 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (INTC, MRVL, EWT, GOOG), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-05), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 35% to 31%, and the regime reading stayed mixed.
